dossier.architecture: Compact turret fed by rotating floor/conical spindexer and curved-rack collection.

subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve; exact module specification unresolved in reviewed team replies.
subsystems.intake: Third collector version adds kicker and articulated secondary kicker; curved rack stays low in stow to preserve capacity.
subsystems.transfer: Cone and rotating floor; separate X44s power spindexer and uptake. Ratios and feeder wheels revised repeatedly; automated recovery clears intermittent jams.
subsystems.scoring: Three-X44 flywheel, no powered top roller; compact turret and hood. Team identifies light printed wheel plus supplemental inertia kit.
subsystems.endgame: Endgame installation not established in reviewed release.
subsystems.controls: Empirically tuned tables plus iterative physics solution compensate motion and spin; local floodlight helps close-range tag shadows, not distant detection.

versions: At least three intake configurations; feed-wheel changes reported seven/eight times.
Do not treat speculative third-party explanations in thread as team-confirmed geometry.
dossier.analysis: A conical spindexer is a different singulation family from a pocketed DYE Rotor. Curved deployment preserves low internal volume; contact friction, congestion and turret interference remain the transfer-critical variables.
limits: Only the reviewed published configurations are established; intermediate changes may be undocumented.

context_documents.title: 2026-9483 · Small turret throughput cannot be inferred from exterior geometry
context_documents.body:
# 2026-9483: Small turret throughput cannot be inferred from exterior geometry

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

First-party replies describe separate X44s for indexer and spindexer, a spinning floor/cone with no deliberate wall compression, and multiple feeder-wheel and ratio trials. The third intake version adds a kicker and movable secondary kicker. The shooter lacks an upper roller; its moving-shot solution combines tuned lookup data and a physics calculation that compensates for spin.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team says the movable kicker resolves earlier collector difficulty and clarifies that the feeder delivers fuel without spin. It does not provide a definitive causal explanation for all of the achieved spindexer throughput. The added flood light helps close-range tag reliability rather than substantially increasing long-range detection.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

The absence of a counter-roller makes spin an explicit aiming input rather than something to assume away. A compact turret may leave more free hopper area, but the detailed explanation of dead zones and geometry offered by another commenter is expressly an outsider’s hypothesis. Keep that hypothesis separate from the team’s replies. Successful self-unjamming also does not mean jams never occur; the source explicitly acknowledges occasional jams.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure entrance spin and moving-shot error across turret angles, record jam/recovery frequency and time, and inspect exact CAD before copying clearances or interpreting an image-based diameter estimate.

## Limits

Selected first-party replies 26, 30, 33, 35 and 47 in topic 515383. Reply 44 is outside analysis, not team intent or a CAD inspection.

source_reviews.title: Team 9483 Presents: Enigma
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the reveal and later team answers through the published discussion and its public post stream.
source_reviews.facts: Team replies describe intake version three, curved rack packaging, independently driven cone and uptake, flywheel construction, empirical shot modeling and close-range illumination.
source_reviews.limitations: Third-party post 44 is conjecture. The written replies give neither final ratios nor a measured CAD envelope.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Enigma puts a rotating-floor conical spindexer below a compact turret. Its intake has to cross the bumper and return inside the robot without raising the rear of the deployment rack through the stored fuel. Separate motors at the rotating floor and uptake provide independent authority over bulk circulation and delivery. The team reports intermittent jams and automatic recovery, making recovery part of the delivered architecture.
source_review.piece_flow: The front collector passes floor fuel into bulk storage. The cone and spinning floor circulate it toward the uptake, then the feeder presents fuel to the turret flywheel. The team describes the feeder as imparting no spin in its reply about perpendicular turret orientation. The launch arrangement lacks a powered top roller, and the aiming model accounts for spin. No final measured throughput curve is provided.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The curved rack keeps its inboard section low while allowing the front roller to descend below the top of the bumper. The team says the articulated secondary kicker barely cleared the depot and encountered no issues at the bump. Those comments support a tight moving envelope at the intake. Clearance through the entire turret sweep at high hopper fill remains an engineering question.

subsystems.name: Collector and rack
subsystems.construction: Curved rack and pinion, front roller, kicker and articulating secondary kicker in the third intake.
subsystems.operation: Rack travel lowers the front roller for acquisition. The secondary kicker can move relative to the primary kicker.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team chose the curve to avoid an elevated inboard rack and preserve hopper capacity.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The path links reach, bumper crossing and stowed intrusion. Impact deflection can change effective gear alignment and field clearance.
subsystems.interfaces: Rack to pinion support, intake-to-bumper clearance and final roller to hopper lip.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: The initial intake was troublesome. Check rack mesh and guide wear through deployment, especially after lateral impact.
subsystems.unknowns: Rack pitch radius, backing material, guide clearance and exact roller stack.

subsystems.name: Spindexer and vertical indexer
subsystems.construction: Cone with spinning floor. One Kraken X44 powers each of the spindexer and vertical indexer.
subsystems.operation: Bulk circulation supplies a separately driven uptake. The robot clears occasional jams automatically.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team iterated ratios and feeder wheels within season time constraints. It reports no designed compression against the hopper walls.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Cone circulation has to keep the pickup supplied without packing a bridge at its entry. Feeder grip and floor velocity are coupled even with independent drives.
subsystems.interfaces: Cone and floor to wall, floor to feeder wheels and feeder outlet to rotating scorer.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Log failed feeds and recovery duration. The team reports seven or eight feeder-wheel changes and denies cone-to-shooter-corner jams in its account.
subsystems.unknowns: Wheel geometry, final ratio, throat compression, detection signal and retry sequence.

subsystems.name: Turret launcher and targeting
subsystems.construction: Three X44 flywheel motors, roughly half-pound three-inch printed wheel and one Thrifty Bot flywheel disc kit per team replies. No powered top roller. Camera has a nearby flood-pattern truck LED.
subsystems.operation: Empirically tuned tables and iterative physics jointly solve moving shots with spin compensation. The light fills close shadows.
subsystems.team_rationale: The light helped close-range tag observations where the net shadowed a tag. The team reports little long-range benefit.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Supplemental inertia can reduce transient droop at the cost of slower setpoint changes. Characterize those effects separately from shot-model residuals.
subsystems.interfaces: Feeder exit to wheel compression, camera to pose estimate and pose/velocity to launch solution.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check printed-wheel balance and fastening after impacts. Measure tag availability with and without the light at representative poses.
subsystems.unknowns: Turret support, hood travel, total inertia and the solver inputs and gains.

revisions: First intake was problematic. Version three added the kicker and a movable secondary kicker. The team also tuned uptake ratios and changed feeder wheels repeatedly without replacing the overall feed architecture.
transferable_principles: Lay out the complete deployment path against the occupied hopper volume. Test rotating bulk feed and throat traction independently at several fill levels.
disconfirming_conditions: The rack benefit shrinks if an equally low linear path fits the same structure. The spindexer transfer case weakens if recoverable jams still consume substantial scoring time at match fill and acceleration.
remaining_gaps: Final drive modules, climbing hardware, gear ratios, recovery logic, and repeatable feed and shot rates by operating state remain unverified.

recommended_images.locator: Team attachments labeled topdown and kickerer
recommended_images.purpose: Review and annotate these candidate figures for the cone-to-feeder path and articulated kicker respectively.
Pair with measured deployed and retracted profiles if a drawing becomes available.
